title: Friendship
note: Friendship helps a ruler in his work, as an army does. He gives it five chapters on what to do and twelve on what to avoid, and this is the first of the five.

couplets.plain: What is as hard to make as friendship? What guard is as hard to get past?
couplets.pm: Nothing is as hard to form as friendship. Finding the right people, the means of winning them, and keeping it unchanged are all hard. Once made, no guard is as hard for enemy action to get past, because enemies fear it and start nothing. Friendship by birth is kin. What he means here is friendship made through past help.

links.quote: What is as hard to make as friendship
links.reason: Calls friendship the hardest thing to make and the hardest guard to get past.

couplets.plain: The friendship of the worthy fills out like the new moon. The friendship of fools wanes like the moon after the full.
couplets.pm: The friendships of the wise fill out day by day like the crescent moon. Those of fools shrink day by day like the moon after the full. Both turn on knowing each other. The wise start small and grow as they come to know each other. Fools start big and shrink for the same reason.

links.quote: The friendship of the worthy fills out like the new moon
fills out like the new moon

couplets.plain: A bond with people of good character is like a book: each time you return to it, it delights you more.
couplets.pm: The friendship good people form with one another delights them each time they meet, as the meaning of a book delights the learned each time they study it. In both, the delight grows from one time to the next.

links.quote: each time you return to it, it delights you more

couplets.plain: You make friends not to laugh together but to step in and rebuke when someone goes too far.
couplets.pm: Friendship isn’t for saying funny things and laughing together. It is for getting in first and rebuking a friend who does what he shouldn’t. An act that brings blame and sin yields only pain, so it is “too far”. It must be stopped before it is done, so you “step in”. Sweet words won’t turn him back, so you “rebuke”.

links.quote: to step in and rebuke when someone goes too far

couplets.plain: There is no need to meet or spend time together. Feeling alone gives the bond of friendship.
couplets.pm: To be friends you needn’t live in one land, or meet and talk often. Feeling the same gives the right of friendship by itself, as with kōpperuñjōḻaṉ and pisirānḍaiyār, who had neither, and yet had a friendship in which they gave up life together. Of the three causes of friendship, the last is the greatest.

links.quote: Feeling alone gives the bond of friendship
links.reason: Puts the strength of friendship in shared feeling, not in hours spent together.

couplets.plain: Friendship that makes the face smile is not friendship. Friendship makes the heart smile deep within.
couplets.pm: A friendship in which only the face blooms on meeting, and not the heart, isn’t friendship. Only the one in which the heart too blooms with loving-kindness is friendship. So both must bloom together.

links.quote: Friendship that makes the face smile is not friendship
links.reason: Separates the smile on the face from the smile deep in the heart.

couplets.plain: Friendship turns you from what would ruin you, sets you on the path, and shares the pain when ruin comes.
couplets.pm: Friendship stops you when you take the bad ways that bring ruin, and drives you onto the good ways when you don’t take them. When ruin comes from the gods and can’t be stopped, it shares that suffering with you. Some read this differently, with a different word, and take the ruin to be the body’s death.

links.quote: Friendship turns you from what would ruin you
links.reason: Gives three marks of friendship: it turns you from ruin, sets you on the path and shares the pain.

links.quote: turns you from what would ruin you, sets you on the path
links.reason: Credits friendship with turning you from ruin and setting you on the path.

links.quote: shares the pain when ruin comes

couplets.plain: Like the hand of someone whose clothes slip, friendship takes away trouble on the spot.
couplets.pm: When a man’s clothes come loose in an assembly, his hand goes at once and saves him from shame. In the same way friendship goes at once to a friend in trouble and removes it. The hand moves faster than the mind when something must be covered, and that speed is the point.

links.quote: friendship takes away trouble on the spot
takes away trouble on the spot
Like the hand of someone whose clothes slip

couplets.plain: Where does friendship sit enthroned? In standing firm, without wavering, and holding you up in every way it can.
couplets.pm: The throne of friendship is the steady support that, without ever changing, holds a friend up in righteousness and wealth as far as it can. These secure the next world and this one. When he falters in them, nothing goes further than lifting him and setting him back, so this is the limit of friendship.

links.reason: Places friendship’s throne in unwavering support, given in every way it can.

couplets.plain: “They are this much to us, and we are this much to them.” Say it, however finely, and the friendship looks poor.
couplets.pm: Two friends may praise each other, saying “He has this much loving-kindness for me, and I am like this to him”, but then the friendship looks shabby. They had no “I” and “he” between them, and even fine words of that sort make a difference where there was none.

links.quote: Say it, however finely, and the friendship looks poor
links.reason: A bond that is spelled out and praised looks poor for all the praise.
